questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: A patient is in a crash airway (imminent arrest, unable to ventilate). What does the RSI guideline allow?
options: Delayed sequence intubation with ketamine first
Five minutes of NRB plus nasal cannula first
questions.explanation: A crash airway is one of the situations for intubation without full RSI; the guideline says to consider paralytics or sedation without pre-oxygenation because there is no time to pre-oxygenate.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: When may delayed sequence intubation (DSI) be considered?
options: Patient is combative or cannot tolerate pre-oxygenation
SpO2 drops below 90% during an intubation attempt
SBP is below 90 despite a fluid bolus
Patient is 28 days of age or younger
questions.explanation: DSI uses a dissociative ketamine dose so a combative patient, or one who will not tolerate the mask, can be adequately pre-oxygenated before paralysis.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: In delayed sequence intubation, the patient received ketamine 1 mg/kg for pre-oxygenation. What additional ketamine is given before paralysis and intubation?
questions.explanation: The DSI dose is only half the induction dose; a further 1 mg/kg brings the patient to the full 2 mg/kg and ensures sedation before paralysis.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: A patient needing RSI is hypotensive from hemorrhage. What resuscitation is directed before any RSI medication?
questions.explanation: Pre-intubation optimization matches the fix to the cause: blood for hypotension from bleeding, fluid bolus for dehydration or sepsis, decompression for tension pneumothorax.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: Before RSI, a patient's hypotension is refractory to fluids and blood. What is used next?
questions.explanation: Vasopressors (push-dose epinephrine) are directed for hypotension refractory to fluids/blood or when an immediate rise in BP is needed, because RSI drugs and PPV can precipitate arrest.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: How should the induction agent be dosed for an RSI patient with hypotension?
questions.explanation: RSI agents cause cardiac depression and loss of sympathetic tone; the pre-intubation optimization step directs a half-dose of ketamine or midazolam in hypotension.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: An adult RSI candidate has a heart rate of 110 and SBP of 120. What is the shock index, and is it positive?
questions.explanation: Shock index is HR / SBP = 110 / 120 = 0.92. For age 13 and older it is positive above 0.9, so this normotensive patient still needs resuscitation before RSI drugs. 1.09 is the ratio inverted.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: A 5-year-old needing RSI has a heart rate of 130 and SBP of 110. What is the shock index, and is it positive?
questions.explanation: Shock index = 130 / 110 = 1.18. For ages 4 to 6 the threshold is > 1.22, so this is not positive; it would be positive under the > 1.0 cut-off used for ages 7 to 12.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: Which induction agent is the drug of choice for most RSI patients?
questions.explanation: Ketamine 1-2 mg/kg IV is listed as the drug of choice for most patients, with a lower dose used in hypotension.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What is the induction dose of etomidate for RSI?
questions.explanation: Etomidate is 0.3 mg/kg IV (may repeat x2), capped at 40 mg adult and 20 mg pediatric; 0.2 and 0.1 mg/kg are the adult and pediatric midazolam doses.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: How many times may the etomidate induction dose be repeated during RSI?
questions.explanation: Etomidate 0.3 mg/kg IV may be repeated x2, within the 40 mg adult / 20 mg pediatric maximums. Succinylcholine, by contrast, is never repeated.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: Why must post-intubation sedation and analgesia be drawn up and ready when etomidate is the induction agent?
questions.explanation: Etomidate's sedation is short; post-intubation sedation and analgesia must be drawn up and ready so the patient is not left under-sedated after the tube is placed.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What is the adult induction dose of midazolam for RSI?
questions.explanation: Adult midazolam induction is 0.2 mg/kg IV (max 20 mg); the pediatric dose is 0.1 mg/kg. Use caution in hypotension.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: After midazolam is given for RSI induction, how long should the crew wait before giving the paralytic?
questions.explanation: Midazolam's slower onset means a three-minute wait before the paralytic, compared with 30 seconds after ketamine and immediately after etomidate.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What is the succinylcholine dose for RSI?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine is 1-2 mg/kg IV to a maximum of 200 mg and is not repeated; it is first line unless the patient is under 10 or has a contraindication.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: An RSI patient's potassium is 6.2 mEq/L. Which RSI drug should be avoided?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine should be avoided when potassium is 6 mEq/L or higher because it raises serum potassium; rocuronium is the alternative paralytic.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What is the IV dose of rocuronium for RSI?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium for RSI is 1 mg/kg IV (or 2 mg/kg IM), max 100 mg. 0.5 mg/kg is the maintenance dose and 1.8 mg/kg is the IM re-initiation dose.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What is the maximum rocuronium dose for RSI?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium (1 mg/kg IV or 2 mg/kg IM) is capped at 100 mg; 200 mg is the succinylcholine maximum.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What does BURP stand for when used to improve glottic view during intubation?
questions.explanation: BURP moves the larynx backward, upward and to the patient's right; it may be combined with external laryngeal manipulation to improve glottic visualization.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: A pediatric patient remains bradycardic during RSI despite adequate re-oxygenation. After stopping the attempt, what atropine dose is given?
questions.explanation: Persistent bradycardia after re-oxygenation means stop the attempt and give atropine: 0.02 mg/kg IV q 3-5 min for pediatrics, 1 mg IV (max 3 mg) for adults.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: A team member has used both allowed intubation attempts without success. What is directed next?
options: Give a second succinylcholine dose and retry
Continue attempting until SpO2 falls below 90%
Awaken the patient and abandon airway control
Re-oxygenate, then further attempts and/or an SGA or cric
questions.explanation: After failed attempts, re-oxygenate before any further attempt and consider alternate airway placement (supraglottic airway or cricothyrotomy).

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: In addition to ETCO2, how many separate techniques must verify ETT placement?
questions.explanation: ETCO2 is mandatory and must be backed by at least two other techniques: breath and gastric sounds, chest rise, SpO2 maintained or rising, tube misting.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: When ETT depth can be visualized, where should the tube sit?
options: Balloon resting at the vocal cords
Balloon about 1 cm past the vocal cords
Cord marker 1 cm past the vocal cords
questions.explanation: Visualizing depth is preferred: pass the balloon about 1 cm beyond the cords or place the cord marker at the cords; otherwise estimate depth by formula.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: An adult who is 72 inches tall is intubated. What is the estimated ETT depth at the incisors by the height formula?
questions.explanation: For patients 5 feet or taller, depth = (height in inches / 4) + 4 = 72/4 + 4 = 22 cm. 18 cm forgets the + 4; 22.5 cm is the < 5 ft rule (3 x a 7.5 tube) misapplied.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: A child under 5 feet tall is intubated with a 5.5 ETT. What is the estimated ETT depth at the incisors?
questions.explanation: Under 5 feet, depth = 3 x ETT size = 3 x 5.5 = 16.5 cm. The distractors use a tube one half-size off (5.0, 6.0) or 4.5.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: What ETT cuff pressure is targeted in a pediatric patient after intubation?
questions.explanation: Check cuff pressure with the manometer: pediatric target 15-20 cmH2O, adult 20-25 cmH2O.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: The crew is told after handoff that their ETT placement was incorrect. What must they do?
options: Amend the chart to state the tube was moved
Immediately notify the CMOC and complete a QM report
Document it at the next quarterly review
questions.explanation: An incorrect placement must be reported immediately to the Clinical Manager on Call (CMOC) along with a QM report.

questions.title: Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI)
questions.stem: Using the RSI nomogram, what ETT size and depth suit a patient 6 feet 2 inches tall?
questions.explanation: The nomogram gives 8.0 mm for patients 5'11" and taller, and a depth of 23 cm at 6'2". 7.5 mm is for 5'3" to 5'10"; 24 cm is the 6'4" depth.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: On the HEAVEN airway assessment, which pre-intubation SpO2 meets the Hypoxemia criterion?
questions.explanation: HEAVEN flags hypoxemia at SpO2 93% or below. Note the separate pre-oxygenation trigger: 94% or below after pre-ox moves to BVM with PEEP.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: What does the Neck item of the HEAVEN airway assessment flag?
options: Size 8 years or under, or obesity
questions.explanation: N = Neck: limited range of motion, which hampers positioning for laryngoscopy.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: What does the Anatomic challenge item of the HEAVEN assessment include?
options: Size 8 years or under, or obesity
questions.explanation: A = Anatomic challenge: trauma, swelling, pregnancy and similar distortions of airway anatomy.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: On the RSI Checklist, the crew answers YES to decreased SBP and/or increased shock index. What does the checklist direct?
questions.explanation: A low SBP or high shock index means resuscitate with fluids, blood and pressors before giving RSI drugs, which can precipitate arrest.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: During RSI Checklist equipment preparation, what status is called for the C-MAC?
questions.explanation: The C-MAC must be recording, which also supports the recorded video confirmation pathway when ETCO2 waveform is inconsistent.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: What is the final item of RSI Checklist equipment preparation, immediately before intubation?
questions.explanation: The equipment section closes with a safety time out prior to intubation, called COMPLETE, after the post-intubation plan is discussed.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: What is the first item on the post-intubation section of the RSI Checklist?
options: Confirm ETT with ETCO2 and lung sounds
questions.explanation: Post intubation runs: confirm ETT with ETCO2 and lung sounds, inflate cuff and secure, sedation/analgesia, then check cuff pressure.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: On the RSI Checklist post-intubation section, what follows inflating the cuff and securing the tube?
options: Confirm ETT with ETCO2 and lung sounds
questions.explanation: After the tube is confirmed and secured, the next callout is post-intubation sedation/analgesia, then cuff pressure is checked last.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: Using the RSI Checklist medication card, what rocuronium dose is given to a 120 kg adult for RSI?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium is 1 mg/kg (120 mg) but capped at a maximum of 100 mg. 240 mg is the IM 2 mg/kg rate and 60 mg the 0.5 mg/kg maintenance rate.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: A 110 kg adult is to receive succinylcholine at 2 mg/kg for RSI. What dose is given?
questions.explanation: 2 mg/kg x 110 kg is 220 mg, but succinylcholine is capped at 200 mg. 100 mg is the rocuronium maximum.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: What etomidate dose is given for RSI to a 150 kg adult?
questions.explanation: 0.3 mg/kg x 150 kg is 45 mg, which exceeds the 40 mg adult maximum. 20 mg is the pediatric maximum; 30 mg uses the midazolam 0.2 mg/kg rate.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: What midazolam induction dose is given for RSI to a 25 kg child?
questions.explanation: Pediatric midazolam is 0.1 mg/kg: 0.1 x 25 = 2.5 mg. 5 mg uses the adult 0.2 mg/kg rate; 7.5 mg the etomidate 0.3 mg/kg rate.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: A 3.5 kg, 2-week-old neonate is to undergo RSI. What atropine pre-treatment dose is given?
questions.explanation: Age 28 days or younger prompts atropine 0.02 mg/kg: 0.02 x 3.5 = 0.07 mg. 1 mg is the adult bradycardia dose.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: Using the RSI Checklist formula, what cuffed ETT size is chosen for a 4-year-old?
questions.explanation: ETT size = (age + 16) / 4 = (4 + 16) / 4 = 5.0, then subtract 0.5 for a cuffed tube = 4.5.

questions.title: RSI Checklist
questions.stem: An 8-year-old under 5 feet tall gets an uncuffed ETT sized by the RSI Checklist age formula. What is the estimated depth?
questions.explanation: Size = (8 + 16) / 4 = 6.0; under 5 feet depth = 3 x ETT size = 18 cm. 16.5 cm uses the cuffed 5.5 tube; 10 cm adds 4 to the size.
